title: Final Practical, Handoff, and RCS Closeout
markdown:
# RCS Day 8 - Final Practical, Handoff, and RCS Closeout
CTS Cohort 6 | CTS Day 16 | 2026-07-30 | 10:00 AM-3:00 PM

## Core rule
A professional does not guess. A professional checks, protects, and verifies.

## Big idea
Competence is the ability to perform safely, explain decisions, verify results, and leave trustworthy evidence for the next person.

## Architecture of the day
| Time | Instructor move |
|---|---|
| 10:00-10:20 | Assessment briefing, PPE, and station boundaries |
| 10:20-10:50 | Final written knowledge check |
| 10:50-12:30 | Measurement, systems, and troubleshooting stations |
| 12:30-1:00 | Lunch and controlled reset |
| 1:00-1:40 | Final capstone wall QC |
| 1:40-2:10 | Evidence index and handoff preparation |
| 2:10-2:40 | Two-minute handoffs and instructor conferences |
| 2:40-3:00 | Reflection, next step, and final reset |

## Learning targets
- Complete the final written knowledge check
- Demonstrate measurement, inspection, and troubleshooting skills
- Present the capstone wall and evidence package
- Complete reflection and next-step planning

## Materials and setup
- Six written assessments, scoring keys, practical rubrics, and clipboards
- Measurement/layout, systems-ID, isolated troubleshooting, and wall-QC stations
- Instructor-controlled fault inserts and station reset materials
- Six capstone walls with student evidence indexes
- Two-minute handoff rubric, timer, and conference notes
- PPE, boundary signage, reflection forms, and final-reset checklist

## Instructor talking points
- Set a calm assessment frame: the goal is valid evidence, not trick questions.
- Review the station boundaries and how students request clarification without receiving answers.
- Explain the capstone rubric: safety, accuracy, system understanding, quality, verification, documentation, and handoff.
- Model a concise professional presentation.
- Close the RCS sequence by connecting strengths and next steps to apprenticeship habits.
